classification.difficultyReason: Combines an absolute value with a rational function and requires separate intervals on either side of an excluded pole.

inlines.text: Compare the absolute-value rational graph with

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\left|\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}\right|$ and $y=3$, with $x\ne-1$.

At their intersections,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x-1}{x+1}&=3\quad\text{or}\quad\frac{x-1}{x+1}=-3\\x-1&=3x+3\quad\text{or}\quad x-1=-3x-3\\x&=-2\quad\text{or}\quad x=-\frac12.\end{align*}$$
The absolute-value graph is on or above $y=3$ between these intersections, except at its pole. Therefore
$$-2\le x<-1\quad\text{or}\quad-1<x\le-\frac12.$$
